04-055.r: Buddha: born at Lumbini in the Shakya clan of Kapilavastu (563 BC); enlightened at Bodh Gaya; rejected Vedas and Vedic rituals; preached noble truths → all four correct.

04-056.r: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya → where Buddha got enlightenment at 35, under a Pipal tree on Vaisakh Purnima, after six years of search.

04-057.r: Present Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya → fifth generation, planted on Alexander Cunningham's orders; king Shashank destroyed the original in the seventh century (Hiuen Tsang).

04-058.r: Bodhgaya (Buddha's enlightenment) → on the bank of River Niranjana.

04-059.r: Buddha's teachings → mainly purity and holiness of conduct.

04-060.r: Wanted to lead the Sangha in Buddha's lifetime → Devadatta, Buddha's cousin; he failed.

04-061.r: Buddha nominated no successor for the Sangha → 'none of the above'; teachings stayed oral; councils settled doctrine by consensus.

04-062.r: Eightfold Path → theme of the Dharma Chakra Pravartana Sutta; the path ends life's misery and leads to Nirvana.

04-063.r: Buddhist philosophy: cause of Samskara (impression) → Avidya (ignorance), the root of all suffering.

04-064.r: Buddha believed in Karma, rebirth (past lives in the Jatakas) and Nirvana; he did not believe in God's existence or power → 1, 2, 3.

04-065.r: Women admitted as Bhikshunis → at Vaishali, on Ananda's request; first woman admitted → Mahaprajapati Gautami.

04-066.r: Tripitaka (Buddhist holy book): Sutta Pitaka → Buddha's sermons; Vinaya Pitaka → rules for Sangha and monks; Abhidhamma Pitaka → philosophy.

04-071.r: 'Yamaka' → Abhidhamma Pitaka (philosophical part of the Tripitaka).

04-072.r: Vinaya Pitaka → rules for the monastic order; Sutta Pitaka → Buddha's teachings; Abhidhamma Pitaka → philosophy; Mahavamsa → regional histories of Buddhism.

04-073.r: Buddha's sermons on ethics and doctrine → Sutta Pitaka; its Digha Nikaya has 34 long Suttas.

04-074.r: Triratna (three jewels) of Buddhism → Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha.
04-074.t: Don't confuse Triratna with Tripitaka (Vinaya, Sutta, Abhidhamma).

04-075.r: Seed of Buddhist philosophy lies in Buddha's own teachings; Buddha stressed moral life over philosophical problems; later scholars built the philosophy → both correct.

04-076.r: Pavarana → ceremony after the four-month rainy-season stay, where monks confess offences and plan future work.

04-077.r: Ashokaram Vihar → Pataliputra; built by Ashoka under monk Indragupta (per Mahavansh).

04-078.r: Vishwa Shanti Stupa (World Peace Pagoda), called the world's highest stupa → Rajgir hills, Bihar.

04-079.r: World's largest and tallest stupa → Kesariya (East Champaran, Bihar): about 104 feet high, 400 feet around; one foot taller than Borobudur.

04-080.r: 80-feet Giant Buddha at Bodhgaya (dhyana mudra; sandstone and red granite) → built with help of the Daijokyo sect of Japan.

04-081.r: Word 'Stupa' first used in the Rigveda, meaning 'tree stem'; anything raised like a heap or pile.

04-082.r: Stupa site not linked to any event of Buddha's life → Sanchi. Bodhgaya → enlightenment; Sarnath → first sermon; Kusinara → death.

04-083.r: Stupa concept predates Buddhism (Rigveda, Atharvaveda) → statement 1 wrong. Stupa = repository of relics and a votive, commemorative structure → only two correct.

04-084.r: Bharhut and Sanchi stupas → built under Ashoka (Dhamekh too, per some sources); Amaravati → Satavahanas; their exact order cannot be fixed.
04-084.c: No answer printed; the book says the order cannot be decided and the question should be excluded.

04-085.r: Great stupa of Amaravati → Satavahana dynasty.

04-086.r: Devnimori Buddhist stupa and monastery (3rd-4th century AD) → Arvalli district, Gujarat.

04-087.r: Anatmavada (no permanent self or soul) → Buddhism; follows from Buddha's Pratityasamutpada.

04-088.r: 'World is unstable and transient' → Buddhism: impermanence (Anitya), one of the three marks of existence.

04-089.r: 'Light of Asia' → Gautama Buddha; Edwin Arnold wrote the book 'The Light of Asia' on his life.

04-091.r: Buddha's epithets → Shakyamuni (sage of the Shakyas) and Tathagata. Nayaputta → Mahavira (24th Tirthankara), not Buddha.

04-092.r: Neo-Buddhism (Navayana, 'new vehicle') → B.R. Ambedkar; stresses social equality; rejects monasticism, karma, rebirth, four noble truths.

04-093.r: Doctrine of momentariness → Buddha (basic principle of impermanence).

04-094.r: 'Paramitas' → perfections a Bodhisattva strives to attain on the path to becoming Buddha.

04-095.r: Edwin Arnold's 'The Light of Asia' (subtitle 'The Great Renunciation', July 1879) → based on the Lalitavistara.

04-096.r: Hinayana vs Mahayana: key difference → treating Buddha as God. Hinayana saw him as a great man; Mahayana worshipped his idols.

04-097.r: Buddha raised to God → Kanishka's period: fourth council split Hinayana and Mahayana; Mahayana worshipped Buddha idols.

04-098.r: First human statues worshipped in India → Buddha (by the Mahayana sect).

04-099.r: Foundation of idol worship in India → Buddhism (Mahayana followers worshipped Buddha images).

04-100.r: Gandharan Buddha image of the Sarnath first sermon → Dharma Chakra mudra; Gandhara art inspired by Hellenistic realism.

04-101.r: Standing Buddha statues → Kushana period (Gandhara art under Kanishka; Mathura school carved sitting and standing Buddhas).

04-102.r: Oldest Buddha sculpture not settled: Mathura (V.S. Agrawal), Kaushambi (Hiuen Tsang), Gandhara (other historians) → 'more than one of the above'.

04-103.r: Bhumisparsha Mudra → Buddha calls the Earth to witness his purity and enlightenment despite Mara's temptations; right hand touches the ground.

04-104.r: Sarnath Buddha image in Bhumisparsha Mudra → Gupta period; the mudra shows steadfastness.

04-106.r: Correct: Parivrajaka → renunciant and wanderer; Upasaka → lay follower of Buddhism. Wrong: Shramana is a wandering ascetic monk, not a high-status priest.

04-107.r: Did not help spread Buddhism → Pushyamitra Shunga (Mauryan general who killed Brihadratha in 185 BCE; persecuted Buddhists). Helped: Ashoka, Kanishka, Harshavardhana.

04-108.r: Kushinagar → capital of the Mallas (a Mahajanapada) and site of Buddha's Mahaparinirvana; A and R true, R not the explanation.

04-109.r: Correct: Lothal → dockyard; Sarnath → first sermon; Nalanda → Buddhist learning. Wrong: Ashoka's Lion Capital is at Sarnath, not Rajgir (Rajgir: hot springs).

04-110.r: Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara (infinite compassion) → also called Padmapani ('lotus-bearer').

04-111.r: 'Aryamanjushrimulakalpa' → Buddhist tantric text linked with Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism.
04-111.c: No answer printed; the explanation links it to both Mahayana and Vajrayana.

04-112.r: Sthaviravadins → Hinayana (not Mahayana). Lokottaravadin → offshoot of Mahasanghika; Mahasanghika deification of Buddha fostered Mahayana → 2 and 3 correct.

04-113.r: Future Buddha yet to come → Maitreya (first in the Cakkavatti Sutta of the Pali Tripitaka).

04-115.r: Bodhisattva Padmapani painting ('one who holds the lotus') → Ajanta, Cave I.

04-117.r: Largest and most evolved Hinayana rock-cut Chaitya hall → Karle (Pune, Maharashtra).

04-118.r: Eleven-headed Bodhisattva image → Kanheri caves (Salsette Island, Mumbai; in Sanjay Gandhi National Park); most caves on a single hill.

04-120.r: Buddhist texts in Sanskrit → Divyavadana and Aryamanjushree Mulakalpa; Deepvamsa and Mahavamsa (India and Sri Lanka history) → Pali.
04-120.t: Deepvamsa and Mahavamsa are Pali chronicles, not Sanskrit.

04-121.r: Indian Buddhist monk sent to China (first century A.D.) → Nagarjuna (book's answer); in Kanishka's court; wrote 'Madhyamikakarika'; called 'Indian Einstein'.

04-122.r: Doctrine of void (Shunyata) → Nagarjuna of the Madhyamika school; key work 'Madhyamikakarika'.
